title: Ice Cream 1.5L

drivers.name: Store closure (Mon)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; 1/7 of week lost. Ice cream is non-essential, so demand drop likely 10-20%. Historical evidence sparse.

drivers.name: Price increase (+2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Price rise from $6.41 to $6.56. Past promotions (10-20% off) lifted sales x1.25 noise-adjusted; small price increase likely suppresses demand by ~5%.

drivers.name: Halloween (event)
drivers.evidence: Historical Halloween weeks: median x1.01, noise-adjusted x1.0. No significant lift observed.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 44.6. Halloween (Sat) has minimal historical lift (x1.01 median, noise-adjusted x1.0), so no meaningful uplift. Store closure on Monday reduces demand: 1/7 of week lost, but ice cream is non-essential; use 0.85 multiplier. Price increase to $6.56 (+2.3%) likely suppresses demand; past 10% off promotions lifted sales by x1.25 noise-adjusted, so a small price rise should reduce demand. Use x0.95 for price. Combine: 1.0 × 0.85 × 0.95 = 0.808. Shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence (one closure, one price change). Final median: 0.88. Downside spread: 1.15 (closure uncertainty), upside: 1.05 (price sensitivity).

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Holiday: Halloween (Sat)
  shelf price: 6.56 (+2.3% vs regular price 6.41)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 44.6 | 5%-95%: 17.1 - 70.6 | 10%-90%: 24.4 - 66.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-36% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
